intro: Guided sequences through the collection. Each trail is a short argument made of passages — read them in order and watch one idea develop.

trails.title: Openings that seduce
trails.blurb: How first sentences make contracts with readers.

stops.note: Three words of command establish intimacy before the drifting begins.
Irony wearing the mask of a universal truth.
Antithesis stacked until a whole age balances on one sentence.
One wrong detail — thirteen — and the world tilts.
Sound itself made complicit; alliteration as seduction.
A sentence holding three tenses at once: firing squad, memory, ice.

trails.title: The rhetoric of protest
trails.blurb: Public speech under pressure, from declaration to refusal.

stops.note: The periodic sentence as a fuse: grievances accumulate toward detonation.
Antithesis and epistrophe compress a war into 272 words.
Balanced clauses refusing vengeance at the moment of victory.
Anaphora as engine: the dream clause returns until it becomes inevitable.
A single periodic sentence made to carry the whole weight of "wait."
Rhetorical questions and refrain as armor and ascent.

trails.title: Shakespeare's balance sheet
trails.blurb: Five speeches, five ways syntax carries a mind under strain.

stops.note: Conditionals and alternatives — logic deployed against an illogical world.
Infinitives without subjects: grammar performing paralysis.
Repetition that goes nowhere, on purpose.
Imperatives hurled at weather; apostrophe at full volume.
Identical structures asserting identical humanity.

trails.title: Grief and consolation
trails.blurb: What form does when feeling would otherwise overwhelm it.

stops.note: Death as courteous coachman; dashes as held breath.
The quatrain as container: form holds the grief so the speaker can.
Suffering placed in the corner of the canvas — understatement as devastation.
The villanelle's returning refrains as refusal.
Litotes rehearsed until it breaks: the art of losing isn't hard to master.

trails.title: The sentence as performance
trails.blurb: Five writers pushing syntax past what prose is supposed to do.

stops.note: The long sentence as an instrument of memory.
Syntax stripped of hierarchy: perception without interpretation.
Polysyndeton as landscape — and, and, and, without mercy.
Fragments doing the work sentences refuse.
A chorus of voices; the sentence dissolved into testimony.

trails.title: First person, singular
trails.blurb: Six narrators whose grammar is their character.

stops.note: Digression as character: the voice that can't stay on topic.
Paradox announced in the first breath: invisible, and telling you.
Direct address as claimed authority: "Reader, I married him."
Flat parataxis: sentences refusing to feel.
The cumulative sentence as a father's unhurried blessing.
Observation sharpened into aphorism.
